name: vbg_balloon_work
prose: Slice cut the head: vbg_balloon_work(work) (vboxguest_core.c:356-415), a workqueue callback. Precondition: work is the mem_balloon.work member of an initialised vbg_dev whose mem_balloon.get_req and change_req buffers are valid. The function does not take a balloon mutex itself; the comments on vbg_balloon_inflate and vbg_balloon_deflate say their caller owns that mutex, and this function does not acquire it, so serialisation comes from the work item being the only caller in the file. Postcondition: returns nothing. It sets req->event_ack and queries the host with vbg_req_perform; if that returns rc < 0 it logs and returns with the balloon state unchanged. If max_chunks is still zero it allocates the pages array with devm_kcalloc(req->phys_mem_chunks entries); on failure it returns silently (no log) with max_chunks still zero and no pages array, otherwise it stores max_chunks = req->phys_mem_chunks. If the host's balloon_chunks exceeds max_chunks it logs and returns with the state unchanged. If balloon_chunks is larger than mem_balloon.chunks it inflates one chunk at a time, and if it is smaller it deflates from the top one at a time; when it is equal neither loop does anything. A failed vbg_balloon_inflate (allocation or host error) frees the pages it allocated for that chunk and records nothing, and a failed vbg_balloon_deflate keeps its pages recorded; either failure makes this function return at once, leaving mem_balloon.chunks equal to the number of chunks completed so far. A successful inflate stores the page array in mem_balloon.pages[i] and increments chunks; a successful deflate frees the chunk's pages and the array, sets the slot to NULL and decrements chunks. When the loop finishes, mem_balloon.chunks equals the host-requested count.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: the work function never locks the balloon mutex (356-409); R2's claim that devm_kcalloc failure logs is wrong, it returns silently (381-383)

name: virtio_mem_run_wq
prose: virtio_mem_run_wq(work) (virtio_mem.c:2415-2502), the workqueue function of a virtio_mem device; work is vm->wq. Postcondition: returns nothing. If vm->in_kdump is set it warns once and returns at once without touching vm->retry_timer, vm->wq_active or anything else. Otherwise it cancels vm->retry_timer with hrtimer_cancel; this happens before the broken check, so a broken device also has its retry timer cancelled. If vm->broken is set it then returns, leaving wq_active untouched. Otherwise it sets vm->wq_active to 1 and loops: it sends an unplug-all request if unplug_all_required is set; if config_changed is set it clears it and refreshes the config (this runs even if the unplug request failed); if the unplug request did not fail it cleans up pending blocks; if that left no error and requested_size differs from plugged_size it sends a plug or an unplug request for the difference; in SBM mode with unplugged blocks pending and no earlier error it sets the result to -EBUSY. The result then selects: 0 resets vm->retry_timer_ms to VIRTIO_MEM_RETRY_TIMER_MIN_MS and arms nothing; -ENOSPC does nothing more and arms no timer; -ETXTBSY, -EBUSY and -ENOMEM arm vm->retry_timer with the current retry_timer_ms; -EAGAIN jumps back to the start of the loop with wq_active still set; any other value logs an error and sets vm->broken to true. After the loop exits (every result except -EAGAIN) it sets vm->wq_active back to 0, including in the broken case.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: hrtimer_cancel is called before the vm->broken return (2428-2431), so the old 'without any work' wording for the broken case was wrong

name: virtio_pci_modern_probe
prose: virtio_pci_modern_probe(vp_dev) (virtio_pci_modern.c:1268-1294); the slice named a function outside it but the function exists in the file. Precondition: vp_dev->pci_dev is set and the embedded mdev has not been probed. Postcondition: it stores vp_dev->pci_dev in mdev->pci_dev and calls vp_modern_probe(mdev). If that returns an error it returns that error at once, without setting any of the callbacks below. Fields of vp_dev->mdev that vp_modern_probe set before failing stay changed (for example mdev->id and mdev->modern_bars, and the mapped-capability pointers, which vp_modern_probe unmaps on its own error labels but does not reset to NULL); the config ops, callbacks, isr, vdev.id and admin_vq lock of vp_dev are not touched in that case. On success it chooses vp_dev->vdev.config as virtio_pci_config_ops if mdev->device is mapped and virtio_pci_config_nodev_ops otherwise, installs config_vector, setup_vq, del_vq and avq_index, copies mdev->isr into vp_dev->isr and mdev->id into vp_dev->vdev.id, initialises the admin_vq spinlock and returns 0.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: vp_modern_probe fills mdev->id/modern_bars/mappings before several failure returns (virtio_pci_modern_dev.c:223-380), so vp_dev is not otherwise unmodified

name: eeprom_write
prose: eeprom_write(filp, kobj, bin_attr, buf, off, count) (w1_ds2433.c:226-275), the write method of the sysfs "eeprom" attribute; the slave is kobj_to_w1_slave(kobj). Precondition: buf is readable for count bytes; the caller does not hold sl->master->bus_mutex. Postcondition: count is first clipped by w1_f23_fix_count: it becomes 0 if off is greater than bin_attr->size, becomes size - off if off + count exceeds size (this is 0 when off equals size) and is otherwise unchanged. If the clipped count is 0 it returns 0 before taking any lock or touching the device (this also covers a request with count 0 and off below size). With CONFIG_W1_SLAVE_DS2433_CRC it then returns -EINVAL, before locking, if off or the clipped count is not a multiple of 32 (W1_PAGE_SIZE), or if any 32-byte block of buf fails the crc16 check (CRC16_VALID is checked against the data in buf, not against the device). It then takes sl->master->bus_mutex and writes the clipped bytes one page-bounded piece at a time with w1_f23_write; a failing piece sets the result to -EIO, stops, and earlier pieces may already be programmed. It releases the mutex and returns the clipped count after all pieces succeed (which can be less than the count requested) or -EIO. In CRC mode each successful piece clears the cached valid-CRC bit of its page.
note: reviewer R15 WRONG: w1_f23_fix_count returns count unchanged for count 0 with off <= size, so 'if (!count) return 0' at line 234-235 runs before mutex_lock (line 253) even when off < size

name: eurwdt_ioctl
prose: eurwdt_ioctl(file, cmd, arg) (eurotechwdt.c:232-297). Precondition: arg is a user pointer: to a buffer of at least sizeof(struct watchdog_info) for WDIOC_GETSUPPORT, to an int for the other commands. The caller does not hold eurwdt_lock, which this function takes (spin_lock) for the hardware operations. Postcondition: the local result starts as -EINVAL. WDIOC_GETSUPPORT returns -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails, otherwise 0. WDIOC_GETSTATUS and WDIOC_GETBOOTSTATUS return put_user(0, p), that is 0 or -EFAULT. WDIOC_SETOPTIONS returns -EFAULT if get_user fails; otherwise, with eurwdt_lock held, WDIOS_DISABLECARD disables the timer and sets the result to 0 and WDIOS_ENABLECARD activates the timer, pings it and sets the result to 0 (both flags run both operations, disable first); if neither flag is set the result stays -EINVAL and is returned. WDIOC_KEEPALIVE pings under the lock and returns 0. WDIOC_SETTIMEOUT returns -EFAULT if copy_from_user fails and -EINVAL if the value is below 0 or above 255; otherwise it stores it in eurwdt_timeout and programs it under the lock, then falls through to WDIOC_GETTIMEOUT, so the new timeout is stored even if the following put_user fails (result -EFAULT). WDIOC_GETTIMEOUT returns put_user(eurwdt_timeout, p). Any other cmd returns -ENOTTY. eurwdt_lock is released before every return that follows taking it.
note: reviewer R15 WRONG: retval is initialised to -EINVAL (eurotechwdt.c:242) and WDIOC_SETOPTIONS with neither flag returns it (255-258), not -ENOTTY; R2 claim was right

name: asr_get_base_address
prose: asr_get_base_address() (ibmasr.c:140-243), an __init function with no parameters that works on the globals asr_type, asr_base, asr_length, asr_read_addr, asr_write_addr, asr_toggle_mask and asr_disable_mask. Postcondition: it first sets asr_length = 1. By asr_type: ASMTYPE_TOPAZ writes 0x07 to ports 0x2e and 0x2f, reads the high and low bytes of the GPIO base from the SuperIO (registers 0x60 and 0x61) and sets asr_base = (high << 16) | low, asr_read_addr = asr_write_addr = asr_base + TOPAZ_ASR_REG_OFFSET and asr_length = 5; the toggle and disable masks are not written. ASMTYPE_JASPER reads the SuperIO base through PCI config ports 0xcf8/0xcfc (asr_base = inl(0xcfc) & 0xfffe), sets the addresses to asr_base + JASPER_ASR_REG_OFFSET, the JASPER masks and asr_length = JASPER_ASR_REG_OFFSET + 1. ASMTYPE_PEARL sets the PEARL base, read/write addresses, masks and asr_length = 4. ASMTYPE_JUNIPER and ASMTYPE_SPRUCE set asr_base to the fixed address, read and write address equal to asr_base and their masks, with asr_length staying 1. For ASMTYPE_UNKNOWN or any other value no case matches: asr_base, the addresses and masks keep their old values and asr_length is 1. In all cases it then calls request_region(asr_base, asr_length, "ibmasr"); if that fails it logs, returns -EBUSY and the globals stay as set above; otherwise it logs the type and address and returns 0 with the region held by the caller, who must release it later.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: ASMTYPE_UNKNOWN sets no masks, so 'masks set for every non-TOPAZ type' was wrong (140-229); JUNIPER/SPRUCE keep asr_length 1, which the old prose did not say

name: sc1200wdt_probe
prose: sc1200wdt_probe() (sc1200wdt.c:321-335), an __init function with no parameters. Postcondition: it calls sc1200wdt_read_data(PMC3, &reg), which takes sc1200wdt_lock, writes the index PMC3 to the index port PMIR with outb_p, reads the data port PMDR into reg and releases the lock; the helper returns void, so reg is written by the call and no read error exists. It then keeps the low nibble (reg & 0x0f) and returns 0 if that equals 0x0e (the PMC3 default value) and -ENODEV otherwise. Apart from the I/O port access it changes no state.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: sc1200wdt_read_data returns void and writes *data unconditionally (sc1200wdt.c:107-112), so the old 'ignored error / uninitialised reg' prose was wrong

name: balloon_wait_finish
prose: balloon_wait_finish() (balloon.c:800-831), registered with late_initcall_sync; no parameters. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV if xen_domain() is false. It returns 0 at once, before logging, if xen_pv_domain() is true or current_credit() (balloon_stats.target_pages - current_pages) is exactly 0. Otherwise it logs a notice and loops while current_credit() is negative: it records the time of the last credit change, and if balloon_state is BP_ECANCELED it warns once and panics when the credit has not changed for balloon_boot_timeout seconds; each iteration sleeps HZ/10 with schedule_timeout_interruptible, so a signal can end a sleep early. When the credit is not negative it logs a completion notice and returns 0. A positive initial credit therefore skips the loop but still prints both notices before returning 0.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: only a zero credit (or a PV guest) returns early (812-813); a positive credit prints the notice and the completion message (815, 829) before returning 0

name: bind_virq_to_irq
prose: bind_virq_to_irq(virq, cpu, percpu) (events_base.c:1360-1419). Precondition: the caller does not hold irq_mapping_update_lock; virq indexes the per-cpu virq_to_irq table and cpu is a valid CPU. Postcondition: it takes the mutex irq_mapping_update_lock and releases it before returning. If per_cpu(virq_to_irq, cpu)[virq] already holds an irq it returns that irq (a WARN fires if its info is missing or not of type IRQT_VIRQ) without any hypercall. If the slot is -1 it allocates an irq_info with xen_allocate_irq_dynamic; on failure it returns -1 (the unchanged slot value). Otherwise it sets the irq chip (xen_percpu_chip with handle_percpu_irq when percpu is true, xen_dynamic_chip with handle_edge_irq otherwise) and calls EVTCHNOP_bind_virq. If the hypercall returns -EEXIST it calls find_virq, which scans the event channels for one bound to this virq and returns 0 with the port when it is bound to this cpu, otherwise -EEXIST if one exists on another cpu and percpu is false, or -ENOENT. Any other nonzero result, from the hypercall or from find_virq, unbinds the new irq with __unbind_from_irq and is returned as is. xen_irq_info_virq_setup is then called; a negative result also unbinds the irq and is returned. On success the irq is bound to the cpu with bind_evtchn_to_cpu and its number (non-negative) is returned.
note: prose of R15-era text verified against lines 1360-1418; contract dropped because it touches global state and the earlier one had no meaning for the cached path

name: gnttab_grant_foreign_access
prose: gnttab_grant_foreign_access(domid, frame, readonly) (grant-table.c:413-424). Precondition: domid names the target domain and frame is the frame to grant. Postcondition: it calls get_free_entries(1), which takes gnttab_list_lock (irqsave), tries to expand the grant table if there are no free entries (gnttab_expand), and removes one reference from the free list. If that call returns any negative value (no entry or the table could not be expanded) this function returns -ENOSPC and grants nothing. Otherwise it calls gnttab_grant_foreign_access_ref(ref, domid, frame, readonly), which writes the entry through the version-specific update_entry op with GTF_permit_access, plus GTF_readonly when readonly is nonzero, and returns the new reference number ref (non-negative). Failed expansion attempts can leave the table grown or the lock-protected counters changed by that attempt, but no entry is claimed.
note: get_free_entries failures of any kind are mapped to -ENOSPC (417-419); prose rewritten without 'exactly'; contract dropped (global grant table state)

name: gnttab_read_frame_v2
prose: gnttab_read_frame_v2(ref) (grant-table.c:484-487), static; returns unsigned long. Precondition: gnttab_shared.v2 is mapped and ref is a valid index into it. Postcondition: returns gnttab_shared.v2[ref].full_page.frame. That field is a uint64_t (include/xen/interface/grant_table.h:204), so the value is converted to unsigned long; on 32-bit builds it is truncated to the low 32 bits, on 64-bit builds nothing is lost. It only reads the shared entry; it takes no lock, changes nothing and does not synchronise with the hypervisor.
note: reviewer R15 WRONG: full_page.frame is a uint64_t (grant_table.h:204), not 32-bit; only the unsigned long return type truncates it on 32-bit builds

name: pcistub_device_id_add
prose: pcistub_device_id_add(domain, bus, slot, func) (pci_stub.c:1106-1144). Precondition: slot and func are each -1 (wildcard) or a plain slot/function number. Postcondition: if slot is negative it calls itself for slots 0..31 with the same func and returns the first nonzero result (or 0), stopping at that point; ids added earlier in the loop remain. If func is negative it does the same for functions 0..7. Otherwise it returns -EINVAL if domain is not in 0..0xffff (in non-module builds, or builds without CONFIG_PCI_DOMAINS, any nonzero domain when pci_domains_supported is false), if bus is not in 0..0xff, or if slot or func does not survive PCI_DEVFN/PCI_SLOT/PCI_FUNC (slot above 31 or func above 7). It then allocates a pcistub_device_id with kmalloc, returning -ENOMEM on failure, and calls pcistub_device_id_add_list, which takes device_ids_lock; if an id with the same domain, bus and devfn is already in the list the new one is freed instead of added. It returns 0 in both cases, so a duplicate request succeeds without adding an entry.
note: old prose omitted that duplicates are freed rather than linked (pci_stub.c:529-556); contract dropped (list state)

name: xen_pcibk_reconfigure
prose: xen_pcibk_reconfigure(pdev, state) (xen-pciback/xenbus.c:362-516). Precondition: pdev is a valid xen_pcibk_device with a valid xenbus device; the caller does not hold pdev->dev_lock. Postcondition: it takes pdev->dev_lock and releases it before returning. The return value is the constant 0 on the exit path shared by all outcomes; the local err is not returned, so errors are visible only through the xenbus state and the log. If the driver state read from pdev->xdev->nodename differs from state it does nothing else. Otherwise it reads num_devs with xenbus_scanf; if that does not return exactly 1 it calls xenbus_dev_fatal (using the negative error, or -EINVAL for a non-negative count) and stops. For each of the num_devs entries it builds "state-<i>" (a name that does not fit 64 bytes calls xenbus_dev_fatal with -ENOMEM and stops) and reads the substate. XenbusStateInitialising reads "dev-<i>" as four hex fields (a read error, a count other than 4, or a name overflow calls xenbus_dev_fatal and stops), calls xen_pcibk_export_device (a failure stops without calling xenbus_dev_fatal in this function), publishes the PCI roots (failure: xenbus_dev_fatal and stop) and writes state-<i> = XenbusStateInitialised (failure: xenbus_dev_fatal and stop). XenbusStateClosing reads "vdev-<i>" the same way and calls xen_pcibk_remove_device (a failure stops, no xenbus_dev_fatal here). Other substates are skipped. After the loop, only when state is XenbusStateReconfiguring, it switches to XenbusStateReconfigured, calling xenbus_dev_fatal if that fails.
note: reviewer R15 WRONG: the function ends with 'return 0' after out: (xenbus.c:505) and err is never returned; the old prose was right on that point but wrongly said export/remove failures call xenbus_dev_fatal here (434-436, 477-479)

name: scsiback_do_1lun_hotplug
prose: scsiback_do_1lun_hotplug(info, op, ent) (xen-scsiback.c:1095-1173). Precondition: info->dev is set; ent names an entry under vscsi-devs in the xenstore; op is any int. Postcondition: it first reads vscsi-devs/<ent>/state into device_state; if the result satisfies XENBUS_EXIST_ERR it returns without writing anything. Any other failure of that read does not stop the function, and device_state may then be unset. It reads p-dev with xenbus_read; if that returns an error pointer it writes XenbusStateClosed to the state node (xenbus_dev_error if the write fails) and returns. It copies p-dev into the local phy buffer (VSCSI_NAMELEN) and frees it. It reads v-dev as four unsigned integers; if that read satisfies XENBUS_EXIST_ERR it writes XenbusStateClosed in the same way and returns; other failures of the scan are not tested. These reads and the Closed write happen for any op value, including unknown ones. It then dispatches: for VSCSIBACK_OP_ADD_OR_DEL_LUN, device_state XenbusStateInitialising calls scsiback_do_add_lun with try = 0, XenbusStateConnected calls it with try = 1 and XenbusStateClosing calls scsiback_do_del_lun; other states do nothing. For VSCSIBACK_OP_UPDATEDEV_STATE with device_state XenbusStateInitialised it writes XenbusStateConnected to the state node; if that write fails it logs, deletes the translation entry for vir and writes XenbusStateClosed, ignoring that result. Any other op does nothing after the reads.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: an unknown op still reads the xenstore and may write XenbusStateClosed on p-dev/v-dev errors (1114-1139), so 'no action' was wrong

name: process_msg
prose: process_msg() (xenbus_comms.c:205-328), no parameters; it keeps its progress in a function-static structure (msg header, body pointer, read count, in_msg, in_hdr flags). Precondition: called from the xenbus reader thread; xen_store_interface is valid. Postcondition: when no message is in progress it sets in_msg, takes xs_response_mutex and holds it until the message is complete or fails; if no data is pending (a save/restore race) it releases the mutex, clears in_msg and returns 0. It reads the header (xb_read); a short header returns 0 with the mutex still held and in_msg set so that the next call continues. A header length above XENSTORE_PAYLOAD_MAX gives -EINVAL, and an inconsistent ring gives -EIO from xb_read; those two cases jump to the common exit, which releases the mutex, clears in_msg, frees the allocated buffer and returns the error. If the kmalloc of the body fails it returns -ENOMEM directly, with xs_response_mutex still held and in_msg still set (the next call retries the allocation). A short body also returns 0 with the mutex held. After a complete body it NUL-terminates it; for XS_WATCH_EVENT it returns the result of xs_watch_msg (the event is handed over and not freed here). For a reply it looks up the request with the same req_id in xs_reply_list under xb_write_mutex: if none is found it returns -ENOENT through the error exit (buffer freed); otherwise it removes it from the list and, if the request is still in xb_req_state_wait_reply, fills in its header and body, sets xb_req_state_got_reply and invokes its callback; a request in another state does not receive the body and the body is not freed here. It then drops a kref on the request, releases xs_response_mutex, clears in_msg, and returns 0 or the watch result.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: partial header/body returns 0 while xs_response_mutex is held and in_msg is set (233-244, 281-285), and -ENOMEM also leaves the mutex held (258-260); old prose said every path releases it

name: pci_acpi_crs_quirks
prose: pci_acpi_crs_quirks() (include/acpi/acpi_drivers.h:74-78) has two variants selected by CONFIG_X86. With CONFIG_X86 the header only declares void pci_acpi_crs_quirks(void); the definition is an __init function in arch/x86/pci/acpi.c:198 that reads the BIOS year from DMI, sets pci_use_crs to false for BIOS years below 2008 when iomem_resource.end is at most 0xffffffff, sets pci_use_e820 to false for year 2023 or later, applies the pci_crs_quirks DMI table and then lets the pci= options (PCI_ROOT_NO_CRS, PCI_USE__CRS) override pci_use_crs. Without CONFIG_X86 it is a static inline function with an empty body, so it does nothing and changes no state.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: only the non-X86 inline stub is empty; the X86 declaration has a real definition in arch/x86/pci/acpi.c:198

name: ACPI_NFIT_BUILD_DEVICE_HANDLE(dimm, channel, memory, socket, node)
prose: Function-like macro ACPI_NFIT_BUILD_DEVICE_HANDLE(dimm, channel, memory, socket, node) (actbl2.h:2191-2196); it expands to an expression with no side effects other than evaluating its arguments once each. Postcondition: the value is dimm | (channel << 4) | (memory << 8) | (socket << 12) | (node << 16), using the ACPI_NFIT_*_OFFSET constants 4, 8, 12 and 16. The arguments are not masked, so a component wider than its field (4 bits for channel, memory and socket and dimm, 12 bits for node) overlaps the neighbouring fields; the type of the result follows the argument types (int arguments shift as signed int, so node values of 0x8000 or more overflow it).
note: macro that builds a value; was dropped as not-a-function but it is a function-like macro with defined behaviour; old contract was an unverifiable macro form

name: ACPI_NFIT_GET_DIMM_NUMBER(handle)
prose: Function-like macro ACPI_NFIT_GET_DIMM_NUMBER(handle) (actbl2.h:2200-2201). The value is handle & ACPI_NFIT_DIMM_NUMBER_MASK, that is handle & 0x0000000F, the low 4 bits of handle in the type of handle (offset 0, no shift). It evaluates handle once and has no other effect.
note: function-like macro; the old prose was right

name: generic___ffs
prose: generic___ffs(word) (asm-generic/bitops/__ffs.h:12-40), a pure function that returns an unsigned int and has no side effects. Precondition: word is nonzero (for 0 the code would return BITS_PER_LONG - 1, which is not a meaningful index). Postcondition: it returns the zero-based index of the least significant set bit of word: it adds 32 (only when BITS_PER_LONG is 64), 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 in turn when the corresponding low group of bits is zero, shifting word down each time. The result is below BITS_PER_LONG, bit result of the original word is 1 and all lower bits are 0.
note: contract reduced to the bit property valid for any width of unsigned long (the earlier one assumed 64 bits and failed in random testing); R2 point that larger values are handled is right

name: ffs(x)
prose: Function-like macro ffs(x) (asm-generic/bitops/builtin-ffs.h:13), defined as __builtin_ffs(x). The argument is converted to int. The value is 0 if that int is 0, otherwise the one-based index of its least significant set bit (1 to 32); an argument whose low 32 bits are zero but whose higher bits are not gives 0 when x is wider than int. It has no side effects.
note: function-like macro forwarding to __builtin_ffs; note int conversion (the old prose assumed x is an int word)

name: ext2_set_bit_atomic(lock, nr, addr)
prose: Function-like macro ext2_set_bit_atomic(lock, nr, addr) (ext2-atomic.h:9-16), a statement expression with a local int ret. Precondition: lock is a spinlock pointer that the caller does not already hold; addr points to a little-endian bitmap that contains bit nr. Postcondition: it takes the spinlock with spin_lock, calls __test_and_set_bit_le(nr, addr) and releases the lock; the value is the previous value (0 or 1) of bit nr, and the bit is 1 afterwards. Other bits of the bitmap are unchanged.
note: slice shows it is a spinlock-protected macro; old prose omitted the lock

name: ext2_clear_bit_atomic(lock, nr, addr)
prose: Function-like macro ext2_clear_bit_atomic(lock, nr, addr) (ext2-atomic.h:18-25), a statement expression with a local int ret. Precondition: lock is a spinlock pointer that the caller does not already hold; addr points to a little-endian bitmap that contains bit nr. Postcondition: it takes the spinlock with spin_lock, calls __test_and_clear_bit_le(nr, addr) and releases the lock; the value is the previous value (0 or 1) of bit nr, and the bit is 0 afterwards. Other bits of the bitmap are unchanged.
note: same as the set variant

name: ffz(x)
prose: Function-like macro ffz(x) (asm-generic/bitops/ffz.h:10), defined as __ffs(~(x)). Precondition: x has at least one zero bit within the width of the complemented value (for an all-ones unsigned long, ~x is 0 and __ffs has no defined result). Postcondition: the value is the zero-based index of the least significant zero bit of x, that is the index of the lowest set bit of ~x.
note: function-like macro; old contract used an ill-formed ACSL expression

name: arch_decode_fprobe_header_size(val)
prose: Function-like macro arch_decode_fprobe_header_size(val) (asm-generic/fprobe.h:41-42), defined only when CONFIG_64BIT is set. The value is (unsigned long)val >> FPROBE_HEADER_MSB_SIZE_SHIFT, where FPROBE_HEADER_MSB_SIZE_SHIFT is BITS_PER_LONG - FPROBE_DATA_SIZE_BITS and FPROBE_DATA_SIZE_BITS is 4 (include/linux/fprobe.h:157), so it yields the top 4 bits of val as a number from 0 to 15. It has no side effects.
note: function-like macro; constants verified in fprobe.h

name: arch_decode_fprobe_header_fp(val)
prose: Function-like macro arch_decode_fprobe_header_fp(val) (asm-generic/fprobe.h:44-46), defined only when CONFIG_64BIT is set. The value is a struct fprobe pointer equal to ((unsigned long)val & FPROBE_HEADER_MSB_MASK) | FPROBE_HEADER_MSB_PATTERN: the low (BITS_PER_LONG - 4) bits of val are kept and the top 4 bits are set to ones (GENMASK(BITS_PER_LONG - 1, FPROBE_HEADER_MSB_SIZE_SHIFT)), so the size bits stored in the top of val are discarded and replaced by the default all-ones pattern. It has no side effects and does not dereference the pointer.
note: function-like macro; old prose said 'fixed MSB pattern', now spelled out

name: find_zero
prose: find_zero(mask) has two definitions in word-at-a-time.h, selected by byte order; it takes an unsigned long mask and returns the byte index (long), with no side effects. Big-endian (lines 26-39): for CONFIG_64BIT the result is 0 for mask >= 2^56, 1 for 2^48 <= mask < 2^56, 2 for 2^40 <= mask < 2^48, 3 for 2^32 <= mask < 2^40, 4 for 2^24 <= mask < 2^32, 5 for 2^16 <= mask < 2^24, 6 for 2^8 <= mask < 2^16 and 7 for mask < 2^8 (including 0); without CONFIG_64BIT the result is 0 for mask >= 2^24, 1 for 2^16 <= mask < 2^24, 2 for 2^8 <= mask < 2^16 and 3 for mask < 2^8. Little-endian (the #else branch, lines 115-118): it returns count_masked_bytes(mask), which for a mask of the form created by create_zero_mask (0, 0xff, 0xffff, up to seven bytes of ones on 64-bit) is the number of low bytes set; the result for other masks follows the formula of the count_masked_bytes definition selected by CONFIG_64BIT.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: the little-endian definition returns count_masked_bytes(mask) (115-118); the old prose described only the big-endian definition, which is correct for that branch

name: count_masked_bytes
prose: count_masked_bytes(mask), 64-bit little-endian definition (word-at-a-time.h:75-78), taking unsigned long mask and returning long; pure. Postcondition: the value is (mask * 0x0001020304050608) >> 56, where the unsigned multiplication wraps modulo 2^64 (that wrapping is intended), so it is the top byte of the wrapped product. For a mask of the form 0, 0xff, 0xffff, 0xffffff, ... (2^(8k)-1 for k from 0 to 7) it equals k; for other masks the formula is evaluated unchanged and has no stated meaning.
note: reviewer R15 MIXED: this item is the 64-bit definition, so the 32-bit-formula objection applies to i=7; the old precondition about not overflowing was wrong because the wrap is intended

name: count_masked_bytes
prose: count_masked_bytes(mask), 32-bit little-endian definition (word-at-a-time.h:83-88), compiled when CONFIG_64BIT is not set; mask is a signed long, the return type is long, pure. Postcondition: with a = (0x0ff0001 + mask) >> 23 (arithmetic shift of a signed value) the value is a & mask. For masks of the form 0, 0xff, 0xffff and 0xffffff it equals 0, 1, 2 and 3 respectively; for other masks the expression is evaluated unchanged. The addition overflows a signed 32-bit long when mask is greater than 0x7fffffff - 0x0ff0001, which is outside the intended masks.
note: 32-bit variant checked by hand for masks 0, 0xff, 0xffff, 0xffffff; the random-test failure at mask=65536 came from comparing it with the 64-bit variant

name: aes_check_keylen
prose: aes_check_keylen(keylen) (include/crypto/aes.h:37-49), static inline; pure. Postcondition: it returns 0 when keylen is AES_KEYSIZE_128 (16), AES_KEYSIZE_192 (24) or AES_KEYSIZE_256 (32), and -EINVAL (-22) for any other unsigned int. It touches no memory.
contract: /*@ ensures ((keylen == 16 || keylen == 24 || keylen == 32) ==> result == 0) && (!(keylen == 16 || keylen == 24 || keylen == 32) ==> result == -22); */
note: prose verified; contract rewritten as two implications

name: einj_cxl_inject_rch_error
prose: einj_cxl_inject_rch_error(rcrb, type) (include/cxl/einj.h:19 and 33-36) has two variants selected by IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_ACPI_APEI_EINJ_CXL). With the option enabled the header only declares int einj_cxl_inject_rch_error(u64 rcrb, u64 type); the definition is elsewhere and is not described here. With the option disabled it is a static inline stub that ignores both arguments and returns -ENXIO (-6).
note: contract kept for the stub only; R2's point that the enabled variant can return other values is right, so the prose now covers both variants (the contract describes the CONFIG-disabled stub)

name: PINMUX2(pin, mux, mux2)
prose: Function-like macro PINMUX2(pin, mux, mux2) (pinctrl-cv18xx.h:12-13). Value: (pin & 0xffff) | ((mux & 0xff) << 16) | ((mux2 & 0xff) << 24). Each argument is masked to its field width (16, 8 and 8 bits), so an out-of-range argument is truncated and cannot disturb the neighbouring fields. Each argument is evaluated once and there are no other effects.
note: function-like macro; the old precondition that arguments fit is not needed because the macro masks them

name: PINMUX(pin, mux)
prose: Function-like macro PINMUX(pin, mux) (pinctrl-cv18xx.h:15-16), defined as PINMUX2(pin, mux, PIN_MUX_INVALD) with PIN_MUX_INVALD equal to 0xff. Value: (pin & 0xffff) | ((mux & 0xff) << 16) | (0xff << 24); the pin and mux arguments are masked to 16 and 8 bits. No other effects.
note: function-like macro

name: PINMUX(pin, mux)
prose: Function-like macro PINMUX(pin, mux) (pinctrl-sg2042.h:10-11). Value: (pin & 0xffff) | ((mux & 0xff) << 16): the pin argument masked to its low 16 bits in bits 0-15 and the mux argument masked to 8 bits in bits 16-23; bits 24-31 are zero. Out-of-range arguments are truncated, not rejected. No other effects.
note: function-like macro

name: PINMUX(pin, mux)
prose: Function-like macro PINMUX(pin, mux) (pinctrl-sg2044.h:10-11). Value: (pin & 0xffff) | ((mux & 0xff) << 16): the pin argument masked to its low 16 bits in bits 0-15 and the mux argument masked to 8 bits in bits 16-23; bits 24-31 are zero. Out-of-range arguments are truncated, not rejected. No other effects.
note: function-like macro

name: virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg(ver, v_opcode, msg, msglen) (virtchnl.h:1661-1892), static inline, with msglen a u16; the name virtchnl_validate_op_msg does not exist. Precondition: ver points to a valid version info (it is read only for VIRTCHNL_OP_GET_VF_RESOURCES); msg is readable for msglen bytes; fields inside msg are read only when msglen is at least the legacy size of the structure for that opcode. Postcondition: it computes the expected length valid_len for v_opcode: a fixed sizeof for most opcodes, zero for opcodes without payload (for example RESET_VF, GET_QOS_CAPS, DISABLE_CHANNELS), sizeof(u32) for GET_VF_RESOURCES when VF_IS_V11(ver) and 0 otherwise, msglen itself for VIRTCHNL_OP_RDMA (a zero msglen is a format error), and for the variable-length messages (VSI queue config, IRQ map, ethernet address list, VLAN lists v1 and v2, RSS key and LUT, RDMA IRQ map, channels, queue bandwidth) the full size computed from the count or length field inside msg when msglen reaches the legacy size. A format error is flagged when num_queue_pairs, num_vectors, num_elements, num_tc or num_queues is zero for the opcodes that test it, or when quanta_size or queue_select.num_queues is zero for CONFIG_QUANTA. VIRTCHNL_OP_EVENT, VIRTCHNL_OP_UNKNOWN and any opcode not listed return VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_PARAM (-5) at once. Otherwise it returns VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_OPCODE_MISMATCH (-38) if a format error was flagged or valid_len differs from msglen, and 0 if not. It only reads its arguments, allocates nothing and takes no locks.
note: slice cut head; real function virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg; the old prose gave the mismatch code as -53 but VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_OPCODE_MISMATCH is -38 (virtchnl.h:50)

name: field_multiplier
prose: field_multiplier(field) (bitfield.h, static __always_inline, taking and returning u64); no side effects. Postcondition: the condition (field | (field - 1)) & ((field | (field - 1)) + 1) is nonzero exactly when field is neither 0 nor a contiguous run of set bits (a run reaching bit 63 passes because the u64 addition wraps to 0, and field == 0 passes the same way). In that nonzero case the code calls __bad_mask(), which is declared __compiletime_error, so a build in which that call remains after constant folding fails to compile; at run time of a call that is reached the function would not return normally. Otherwise it returns field & -field, the lowest set bit of field (0 when field is 0).
note: reviewer R15 unreviewed; prose verified: field==0 and masks that include bit 63 do not call __bad_mask, and the call is a compile-time error only when it survives optimisation

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32_encode_bits(v, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32) in bitfield.h), static __always_inline __must_check, with u32 parameters and a u32 result. Precondition: field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits (a run may include bit 31); for field == 0, field_mask divides by field_multiplier(0) == 0. If v is a compile-time constant with bits outside field_mask(field), the call to __field_overflow() makes the build fail. Postcondition: it returns (v & field_mask(field)) * field_multiplier(field) converted to u32 (no byte swap for the u32 variant): the low bits of v that fit in the field, moved to the field's position, with all other bits zero. It has no side effects.
note: name is the macro invocation that generates the function; division by zero for field 0 added to the precondition

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32_replace_bits(old, val, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32)), static __always_inline __must_check; u32 parameters and result. Precondition: field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits; a constant val that does not fit makes the build fail through __field_overflow(). Postcondition: it returns (old & ~field) | u32_encode_bits(val, field): the bits of old selected by field are replaced by the low bits of val that fit, moved into position, and all other bits of old are unchanged. It has no side effects.
note: name is the macro invocation that generates the function

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32p_replace_bits(p, val, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32)), static __always_inline, returning void. Precondition: p points to a writable u32; field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits; a constant val that does not fit makes the build fail through __field_overflow(). Postcondition: it stores (*p & ~field) | u32_encode_bits(val, field) in *p, so only the bits selected by field change, and returns nothing. The read and write of *p are not atomic.
note: name is the macro invocation that generates the function

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32_get_bits(v, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32)), static __always_inline __must_check; u32 parameters and result. Precondition: field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits (for field == 0 the division by field_multiplier(0) == 0 is undefined). Postcondition: it returns (v & field) / field_multiplier(field): the bits of v selected by field shifted down so the lowest bit of the field is bit 0. It has no side effects.
note: contract simplified to the formula with the lowest set bit; the contiguity requirement is stated in prose
